A Song / Video switch for YouTube Music, and video decoding on the GPU. Website and docs: https://bong-water-water-bong.github.io/ytui/

## Download

| Platform | Package | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `ytui-v2026.10.21-windows-x86_64.zip` | Unzip and run `ytui.exe` in **Windows Terminal**. |
| Linux (x86_64) | `ytui-v2026.10.21-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `ytui-v2026.10.21-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | |

Each package holds `ytui` (or `ytui.exe`), `README.md`, `LICENSE` and `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md`. You also need `yt-dlp`, `ffmpeg` and a JavaScript runtime (`deno` or Node.js) on your PATH, and a truecolour terminal. On Windows: `winget install yt-dlp.yt-dlp Gyan.FFmpeg DenoLand.Deno`.

Checksums are in `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## What's new

- **Song / Video switch:** the YouTube Music player shows **♪ Song** and **▶ Video** buttons when the song you're playing also has a music video, or the video also has an audio track. Switching keeps your place in the song and in the queue. ytui uses the pairing YouTube Music sends when you're signed in, and otherwise searches for the other version, accepting only the same title and lead artist, the same recording (a live or remix version doesn't count) and a matching length.
- **Video decoding on the GPU:** ffmpeg now decodes video with your graphics card (VAAPI on Linux, VideoToolbox on macOS, D3D11VA on Windows), which roughly halves its CPU use. If your GPU or driver can't decode, ytui switches to software decoding and says so; `--hwdec off` always decodes in software.
